title: Locally finitely presented morphisms with unique infinitesimal lifts are etale
statement: Let $c:W\to Z$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that for every first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of affine schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], every pair of scheme morphisms $a_0:T_0\to W$ and $b:T\to Z$ with $c a_0=bj$ admits exactly one morphism $a:T\to W$ satisfying $aj=a_0$ and $ca=b$. Then $c$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02HM, lemma-etale-formally-etale, implication (2) to (1), with Tag 02HG, definition-formally-etale, the unique-lifting formulation for affine first order thickenings.

proof.text: Fix $w\in W$. Choose an affine open $V\subseteq Z$ containing $c(w)$ and an affine open $U\subseteq c^{-1}(V)$ containing $w$. Such choices use the affine-open basis of a scheme. Put $R=\mathcal O_Z(V)$ and $A=\mathcal O_W(U)$. The given locally finite presentation of $c$ implies that the induced $R$-algebra $A$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. We shall show that this affine chart is étale.

source.place: Tag 02HM, lemma-etale-formally-etale, converse proof, affine reduction; morphisms.tex Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize.

proof.text: The unique lifting hypothesis passes to $c|_U:U\to V$. Indeed, given $T_0\hookrightarrow T$, $a_0:T_0\to U$, and $b:T\to V$, compose with the inclusions into $W,Z$ and use the hypothesis to obtain $a:T\to W$. A first order thickening has the same underlying space by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], so every point of $a(T)$ already belongs to the image of $a_0$, hence lies in $U$. Restrict the continuous map of $a$ to $U$ and restrict its structure-sheaf map along $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_W|_U$; this gives a morphism $T\to U$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The equations hold as maps into $U,V$ since the inclusions are injective on points and identify the restricted sheaves. Any two such lifts have identical composites into $W$ by the original uniqueness, and therefore identical continuous and sheaf maps into $U$. Thus the restricted lift is unique.

source.place: Tag 02HK, lemma-formally-etale-on-opens, proof; expanded directly using the definitions.

proof.text: Let $D$ be any commutative $R$-algebra, $I\subseteq D$ an ideal with $I^2=0$, and $u:A\to D/I$ an $R$-algebra map. Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(D/I)$. The quotient induces a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its defining ideal is square zero, so this is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. The map $u$ gives $T_0\to U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By the previous step it has a unique lift $T\to U$ over $V$. By the unique ring-map description of morphisms between spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], this is exactly a unique $R$-algebra map $v:A\to D$ whose composite with $D\to D/I$ is $u$: functoriality of Spec identifies the two required commutative triangles with these ring equations.

source.place: Tag 02HL, lemma-affine-formally-etale, proof, using algebra.tex Tag 00UQ; affine anti-equivalence expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-ring-square-zero-lifts-cotangent-zero] to the unique lifts established in step 3. It gives $\Omega_{A/R}=0$ and $H_1(L_{A/R})=0$. Together with the finite presentation from step 1, these are exactly the three ring conditions in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. Its reverse implication therefore shows that $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is étale.

source.place: Tag 02HM, lemma-etale-formally-etale, converse proof, ring criterion (algebra.tex Tag 00UR); morphisms.tex Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, affine comparison.

proof.text: For every $w\in W$ we have produced affine open neighbourhoods $U$ of $w$ and $V$ of $c(w)$ such that $c(U)\subseteq V$ and the induced affine morphism is étale. The affine-local formulation in [def-weil-etale-morphism] (Stacks Definition 02GI) is precisely that a morphism has such charts at every point. Consequently $c$ is étale. If $W$ is empty the same pointwise criterion is vacuous, so the conclusion also covers this case.

source.place: Tag 02GI, definition-etale, clauses (1)-(2), as recorded in def-weil-etale-morphism.
